raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Purpose

DeepSeek-V3.2 and GLM-5.3 don't run on gfx11. For sparse MLA, `ROCM_AITER_MLA_SPARSE` is the only backend on offer, and its default path needs AITER's MLA kernels, which have no gfx11 build. On current main the server starts, but the first request fails in AITER's `get_mla_metadata_v1`:

```
RuntimeError: [module_mla_metadata] was built against a different pybind11 ABI
than module_aiter_core, so it cannot see the aiter_tensor_t registration ...
```

The Triton sparse path in the same file already handles the 512 + 64 RoPE layout, but `_use_rocm_sparse_triton()` only picks it when `head_size == kv_lora_rank`. This PR lets gfx11 take that path too.

Long-context decode on this path goes through the split-K BF16 kernel from #58584, which needs #61774 for the 576-wide layout. Without #61774, decode past 512 tokens fails with `arange's range must be a power of 2`.

Tests: one new routing test for the gfx11 case, and the existing routing tests now pin `on_gfx11` to `False` so they also pass on gfx11 hardware.

## Duplicate-work check

Searched open PRs and issues for `rocm_aiter_mla_decode_fwd`, GLM-5.3 and DeepSeek-V3.2 on gfx11, and sparse MLA fallback on ROCm. No duplicate.

- #61774 fixes the split-K reduction for non-power-of-two head dims. It is needed together with this PR for long-context decode.
- #52970 is about DeepSeek-V4 and AITER's Triton kernels. It does not touch `_use_rocm_sparse_triton`.

## Test Result

Tested on 4x Strix Halo / Radeon 8060S / gfx1151 with `TP=4`, ROCm nightly wheel, with #61774 applied.

```
vllm serve Tech2wild/GLM-5.3-Int4-Int8Mix \
    --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
    --distributed-executor-backend ray \
    --max-model-len 32768 \
    --max-num-batched-tokens 512 \
    --enforce-eager
```

Before: the first request fails with the error above.

After:

```
"What is 17 times 23?"                      -> 17 × 23 = 391
needle in a ~1.7k-token prompt               -> correct
split-K decode (16 splits at 2048 tokens)    -> runs, matches single-pass
```

```
pytest tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_glm5next_sparse.py
  35 passed
```

## AI assistance

AI assistance was used for this change. The submitting human has reviewed every changed line and ran the tests reported above.

Following up on @amd-xavierwang's gfx1201 question. 
I tested GLM-5.3 sparse MLA on R9700 (gfx1201). With aiter disabled (default), initialization fails in the DSA indexer. With aiter enabled, the default path fails in `get_mla_metadata_v1` (`hipErrorInvalidValue`).

A local gfx12 triton routing change allows short requests to run, but long-context split-K decode hits `tl.arange(0, 576)` compilation error, same issue I reproduced on gfx1100 with this PR's routing change.

I opened #61774 to fix this. With both changes, E2E inference succeeds on gfx1100 and gfx1201 (with some environment workarounds).

@abdmalik-amd, did your gfx1151 test exercise the split-K path (`decode_num_splits > 1`)?
I just noticed that this branch is based before #58584 which added the BF16 split-K decode path, so your gfx1151 run couldn't have reached it. It should show up once you rebase.

> Following up on @amd-xavierwang's gfx1201 question. I tested GLM-5.3 sparse MLA on R9700 (gfx1201). With aiter disabled (default), initialization fails in the DSA indexer. With aiter enabled, the default path fails in `get_mla_metadata_v1` (`hipErrorInvalidValue`).
> 
> A local gfx12 triton routing change allows short requests to run, but long-context split-K decode hits `tl.arange(0, 576)` compilation error, same issue I reproduced on gfx1100 with this PR's routing change.
> 
> I opened #61774 to fix this. With both changes, E2E inference succeeds on gfx1100 and gfx1201 (with some environment workarounds).
> 
> @abdmalik-amd, did your gfx1151 test exercise the split-K path (`decode_num_splits > 1`)?

No, the original gfx1151 run was on a branch from before #58584, so it never reached split-K. After rebasing I hit the same tl.arange(0, 576) compilation error on gfx1151 (4x Strix Halo, TP=4, GLM-5.3) on a ~6k-token request, so I can confirm the issue. Thanks for opening [vllm-project/vllm#61774](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61774). I'll keep this PR to the routing change and note that long-context decode depends on [vllm-project/vllm#61774](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61774).
@JartX @tjtanaa @dllehr-amd can you take a look at this PR when available?
Thanks for confirming! I will note it in #61774 as well.
